dos: Lead with the occasion, not the product — 'The Tuesday board presentation' not 'This blazer'
Subject lines under 50 characters — specific beats generic — name the moment or the problem solved
Name each look with a specific moment: 'The Closing Meeting', 'Friday at 6', 'The Red-Eye Back'
Give each look an angle that explains the styling logic — why these pieces together, not just what they are
Use 3-4 looks per email so the woman sees herself in at least one scenario
Always pair a structured top with something softer underneath (knit, silk, fluid blouse)
Mention the specific products' key attribute — 'the stretch-wool trouser' not just 'trousers'
donts: Never use: effortless, fresh, trendy, hot, chic, stunning, must-have, elevated, sophisticated
Don't list products without styling context — every piece needs a reason to be in the look
No all-black looks described as a 'look' — it's too generic unless the pieces have interesting contrast in texture
Don't float a single hero product without showing what it pairs with
Avoid subject lines starting with 'Your' — too generic and low-open-rate
No discount language, no urgency via scarcity, no countdown language
Don't mix warm and cool tones in a look without a deliberate reason stated
Never two boxy or structured pieces together without a fitted element to balance
toneNotes: Authoritative, not aspirational — she already has authority, this confirms it
Short declarative sentences. Period. Not exclamation points.
Anne Klein woman is 35-55, professionally accomplished, dresses for impact not trend
She buys fewer pieces but wears them more — quality and versatility over quantity
Write like a trusted stylist who knows her wardrobe, not a brand talking at her

dos: Open with a hook that names a specific moment or problem — 'The meeting that ran long'
Conversational, present tense — 'This blazer goes from...' not 'This blazer can go from...'
Reference specific product details — 'the notch collar', 'the patch pocket', 'the pleated front'
Max 5 hashtags — specific beats generic (#WorkwearWednesday over #Fashion)
Imagery direction should be specific: 'Flat lay on marble, navy blazer folded over ivory blouse, camel trouser, nude pump' not 'woman in blazer'
donts: Don't restate what's visible in the image
Avoid 'head-to-toe' outfit descriptions that read like a receipt
toneNotes: More casual than email but never breathless
Intrigue over information — make her tap 'more'
The woman is scrolling, not actively shopping — catch her mid-scroll with a specific, unexpected detail

avoid: All-black without texture contrast — too generic
More than 3 colors in a single look
Neon or bright accents against AK's muted base palette

outfitLogic: Blazer + matching trouser = suiting look — needs a soft element underneath (silk blouse, knit)
Blazer + contrasting pant = modern mix — textures must vary (tweed jacket, crepe trouser)
A structured jacket always needs a soft underneath — never two stiff layers
A fluid midi dress stands alone — don't overcomplicate with a jacket unless the occasion calls for layering
Heels elevate any trouser look for business; block-heel or flat for travel/casual reads
Statement earrings finish any look — AK jewelry should always appear in email looks
Shoes are mandatory in any 'full look' — never show a complete outfit without footwear
occasionFraming: Boardroom / presentation: structured blazer, polished trouser or pencil skirt, low/block heel
Client lunch: blazer or cardigan over blouse, tailored pant, simple jewelry, comfortable heel
Work travel: wrinkle-resistant pieces, layerable, 1 blazer that works day+night
Friday/end of week: blazer off, fluid blouse or knit, same tailored trouser — dressed down not dressed out
Evening/event: midi dress or wide-leg pant + silk blouse, statement jewelry, heels
Weekend with polish: clean trouser or straight-leg denim (not in AK catalog — avoid), knit top, loafer or flat
